context:
Goal: the handoff is current when a cloud session compacts.
Problem (rule): each cycle has one handoff checkpoint, 83k-108k tokens of work before the real compaction, so that work is missing from the handoff when the session resumes.
Based on (measured): the coordinator's window is 480k tokens and it compacts at 442k; the hook's own threshold is 408k; its one checkpoint fired at about 334k.
Based on (read): the hook rewrites the handoff once per cycle, 50k tokens before its own threshold, as the compaction-handoff decision sets.
Departs from: main (one checkpoint 50k below the hook threshold) — adds a second, late checkpoint 20k below it when the first one fired more than 75k earlier.
Why yours: it adds a rewrite to every standing session's cycle, which costs tokens each time.

lastAnswer.note: is our setup script bad? i thought nudges to rewrite handoff trigger multiple times before compaction snd then theres snother trigger after compsction?

options.gain: The last handoff rewrite lands within about 20k tokens of compaction, so little work is lost.
options.how: The hook adds a late checkpoint 20k below its threshold when the first one fired more than 75k earlier.
options.label: Add the late checkpoint (recommended)
options.lose: One more handoff rewrite per cycle, about 10k tokens.

options.gain: No extra rewrites; no added token cost.
options.how: The hook stays as it is; the after-compaction audit agent (PR #3062) catches what the handoff missed.
options.label: Rely on the after-compaction audit
options.lose: The handoff stays stale until the audit runs after compaction.

reply: 00:54 CST Nov 13, the lane's answer: the setup is fine; the hooks are installed in the cloud (checked). But a cloud session gets one nudge, not several. The nudge counts only message tokens, and each session starts with about 88k tokens of fixed load, so with compaction at 384k there is room for one checkpoint (about 334k); the 200k one is dropped as too close. In the coordinator's case the last nudge came about 84k tokens before the real compaction, and everything after it was in no handoff (this matches the retrospective's handoff being about 2 h behind). Option a adds a second nudge about 20k below the line, costing one more rewrite (about 10k tokens) per cycle. The lane still recommends a. Pick a or b on this item.
title: Add a second, late handoff checkpoint before a cloud session compacts?
why: It adds a token cost to every standing session's compaction cycle.
